root_cause_analysis.symptom: Three residual races in daemon auto-upgrade handoff: (F1) stopDaemon() has two independent reads of daemon.state.json — one for PID (line 198) and one for port via daemonPost (line 15) — so HTTP stop can target a different daemon generation than SIGKILL; self-kill via SIGKILL cannot occur at startup because the new daemon writes its own PID at run.ts:664 AFTER calling stopDaemon() at run.ts:119; (F2) cleanupDaemonState() is called before releaseDaemonLock() at TWO sites (run.ts:763-766 heartbeat handoff AND run.ts:831-835 cleanupAndShutdown), AND clearDaemonState() in persistence.ts deletes the lock file it does not own; (F3) all subsystems (apiMachine, controlServer, state, lock, heartbeat) are torn down before spawnHappyCLI is called at run.ts:769; on spawn failure the daemon is a zombie with no control path; process.exit(1) is required in the catch block so the system supervisor can respawn
root_cause_analysis.root_cause: F1: daemonPost() re-reads daemon.state.json independently on every call (line 15) to get the HTTP port, while stopDaemon() captures state.pid at line 198 for SIGKILL; if state.json changes between these two reads the HTTP stop and SIGKILL target different daemon generations. The call-order at startup prevents self-kill: stopDaemon() fires at run.ts:119 before writeDaemonState() at run.ts:664, so state.json still holds the old PID when stopDaemon() runs. The self-kill guard (state.pid === process.pid) remains valid as defense against a future race where state.json updates before SIGKILL at line 220. F2: clearDaemonState() owns lock deletion it does not hold (persistence.ts:325-332); cleanup call order is wrong at both heartbeat handoff (run.ts:763-766) and cleanupAndShutdown (run.ts:831-835) — state before lock, should be lock before state. F3: complete teardown runs before spawnHappyCLI (run.ts:763-767); the existing process.exit(0) is outside the try block at line 778 (unconditional); on spawn failure no subsystems remain and the zombie has no control path; correct fix is process.exit(1) in catch block so systemd Restart=on-failure can respawn.
root_cause_analysis.why_introduced: The upgrade handoff is a complex multi-step teardown sequence; the race conditions were not fully modeled in the prior fix
root_cause_analysis.why_problematic: F1 can cause the new daemon to immediately kill itself during startup. F2 can cause releaseDaemonLock to delete a lock held by a new process. F3 leaves the system with zero daemon processes.
